steps: Learn the key family members in masculine/feminine pairs
Practice describing physical appearance using avoir and être
Write full sentences combining family, possessives and descriptions
method_card.title: Family Members and Descriptions
method_card.content:
This lesson covers family vocabulary, possessive adjectives and physical/personality descriptions.

FrenchEnglish
le pèrefather
la mèremother
le frèrebrother
la sœursister
le grand-pèregrandfather
la grand-mèregrandmother
l'oncleuncle
la tanteaunt
le cousin / la cousinecousin
le filsson
la filledaughter
le beau-pèrestepfather
la belle-mèrestepmother

Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they describe, not the owner: mon (m), ma (f), mes (pl) = my; son (m), sa (f), ses (pl) = his/her. Exception: before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, use mon/ton/son instead of ma/ta/sa.

Physical descriptions: Use avoir for hair and eyes (J'ai les cheveux blonds), être for build and personality (Elle est grande et sympa). Adjectives must agree in gender and number.

Model: Mon père s'appelle Marc. Il a les cheveux courts et bruns. Il est grand et sympa. Ma mère est petite et très gentille.

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — appears in every exam series

bullets.note: il y a + number + dans ma famille, possessive adjectives
bullets.prompt: Say how many people are in your family and name them.
bullets.model_answer: Il y a cinq personnes dans ma famille : mon père, ma mère, mes deux frères et moi.

bullets.note: avoir for hair/eyes, être for build, adjectival agreement
bullets.prompt: Describe your brother or sister's appearance.
bullets.model_answer: Mon frère a les cheveux courts et bruns et les yeux bleus. Il est assez grand.

bullets.note: être + feminine adjective agreement (gentille, amusante, intelligente)
bullets.model_answer: Ma mère est très gentille et amusante. Elle est aussi très intelligente.

bullets.prompt: Say who you get on well with and why.
bullets.model_answer: Je m'entends bien avec ma sœur parce qu'elle est sympa et drôle.

gold.question: Find and fix the grammatical error
gold.sentence: Son père a les cheveux blonds mais son mère est brune.
gold.explanation: mère is feminine, so the possessive adjective must be sa (not son). Son is used before masculine nouns or feminine nouns starting with a vowel.
gold.translation: His father has blond hair but his mother is brunette.

bronze.question: Complete the sentence with the correct possessive adjective
sentence_parts: mère s'appelle Sophie. J'ai deux frères —

wrong.yeux: yeux means eyes, not hair. Les cheveux = hair.

gaps.correct_explain: cheveux means hair — les cheveux longs = long hair.

wrong.vert: vert is singular — les yeux is plural, so the adjective needs the plural form verts.

gaps.correct_explain: verts means green — any eye colour is acceptable here.

wrong.grand: grand is masculine — ma sœur / elle is feminine, so you need grande.

gaps.correct_explain: grande is the feminine form because elle is feminine.

wrong.a: a is from avoir (to have). For descriptions of personality/build, use être.

silver.question: Put these words in the correct order to form a sentence

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break the sentence into chunks: Mon frère | a les cheveux noirs | et | il est assez grand.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Mon frère = My brother. a les cheveux noirs = has black hair (avoir for physical features).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: il est assez grand = he is quite tall (être for build).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: My brother has black hair and he is quite tall.

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Mon frère a les cheveux noirs et il est assez grand.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Look at the noun you are describing — is it masculine, feminine or plural?

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Masculine singular → mon (mon père). Feminine singular → ma (ma mère). Plural → mes (mes parents).

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Exception: feminine noun starting with a vowel → use mon for pronunciation. Example: mon amie (not ma amie).

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: The possessive adjective agrees with the gender/number of the thing owned, not the owner. Mon (m), ma (f), mes (pl), with the vowel exception.
